author: Carena Liptak
title: Zach Bryan Reveals He's Nearly Two Months Sober - NewsBreak
text:
By Carena Liptak ,
14 days ago Jason Kempin, Getty Images Zach Bryan says he hasn’t touched alcohol in nearly two months.
The singer shared the milestone on social media as part of a larger reflection about working on his mental health. Bryan explained that the pressures of fame — and being at the center of public controversy — intensified his anxiety, and he decided to seek therapy to break a cycle of using alcohol as a coping mechanism.
“I haven’t touched alcohol for nearly two months now — something I had to do for my own personal clarity,” Bryan wrote. “I needed to see the world objectively.”
Why Did Zach Bryan Stop Drinking? In his post, Bryan says that he realized he needed to make a change during a recent cross-country motorcycle trip.
“At the end of this ride, I was sitting in a parking lot in Seattle, Wa. thinking ‘I really need some f–king help,'” he remembers.
He says that between his decade of military service and his rise to a level of musical superstardom that he “hadn’t fully comprehended the scope of,” he picked up the motto “to charge forward and never settle” — no matter the cost to his mental health.
Read More : 18 Country Stars Who Are Committed to Sobriety
“I was stuck in a perpetual discontent that led me to always reaching for alcohol, not for the taste, but because there was a consistent black hole in me always needing its void filled,” Bryan continues.
His career put him in the public eye, and not always in a positive way. Bryan says he was “lied about and doxxed on the Internet.”
The singer has been embroiled in a few different feuds with other public figures, the most talked-about of which is with his ex-girlfriend Brianna Chickenfry. She accused him of abuse and claimed he offered her $12 million to sign an NDA promising not to talk about their October 2024 breakup.
Read More : A Full Timeline of Zach Bryan + Brianna Chickenfry’s Breakup
Bryan says that while he was being attacked online, he was also maintaining a relentless touring schedule and helping two friends navigate serious mental and physical health challenges.
“I was having earth-shattering panic attacks,” he admits. “The anxiety I felt was paralyzing, and I thought that since I was successful, had the money I always longed for and had great friends, that I could tough it out.”
How Did Zach Bryan Make a Change in His Mental Health? Bryan says he started working with a therapist to address his “toxic relationship with booze” and “how I cope with major life changes.”
Those closest to him supported his decision, including his girlfriend Samantha Leonard, who he says was a factor in why he decided to stop drinking.
Read More : Meet Zach Bryan’s Girlfriend, Samantha Leonard
“Conversations about the future, kids one day, my health and Sammy’s happiness made me prioritize not only myself, but my entire family,” Bryan explains.
Leonard responded with a comment on Bryan’s post, writing, “I love you my sweet boy.”
Is Zach Bryan an Alcoholic? Bryan described a complicated relationship with habits, addiction and alcohol in his update. He never directly called himself an alcoholic, nor did he say for sure that he’s making a lifelong commitment to swearing off booze.
“I don’t believe in absolutes,” he said at the end of his post.
“One day maybe, I’ll learn to control my habits,” he continued. “But for now I just want to say it is okay to be weak at times and need help. God speed everyone! I pray this helps somebody.”
How is Zach Bryan Doing Today? Bryan’s post makes it seem like the singer’s mental health is better than it has been in a long time.
“I feel great, I feel content, I feel whole,” he wrote. “There is nothing I need to get me by anymore.”
He also hopes his story will reach others who may be struggling.
“If you or any of your friends are too tough, too scared or too stubborn to reach out, know that the most stubborn dumba– on the planet did and didn’t regret it,” the singer adds.
18 Country Artists Who Are Sober Although country music is known for its raucous drinking songs, several artists have sworn off the stuff completely. Be it a lifestyle change or a life-saving decision, each one of these artists can say that that their lives have changed for the better since giving up the bottle. They are sober and proud. Erika Goldring, Getty Images Ashley McBryde While many people knew that Ashley McBryde enjoyed a good drink, hardly anyone knew that she was kicking the habit to the curb. She quietly cut out alcohol in 2022 after realizing her dependency on it, but didn’t really say anything until she had passed a year of sobriety. Her reason was simple: She didn’t want to go public with something she might fail at. But now, she says sober is a wonderful lifestyle. Terry Wyatt, Getty Images Brad Paisley Brad Paisley was pulled over for a suspected DUI in 2011. The caveat? He wasn’t drunk. He had been out getting ice cream with his kids, who were ecstatic to tell everyone of dad’s arrest. The truth is, Paisley is clean as a whistle. Despite writing the classic drinking song "Alcohol," he admits that he doesn’t drink or smoke. His only vice in life is his guitar. Catherine Powell, Getty Images Brantley Gilbert Brantley Gilbert’s problems with drugs and alcohol began shortly after high school, and he continued to struggle until 2011. In fact, he still remembers the last day he had a drink: Dec. 18, 2011. Gilbert credits Keith Urban with helping him get sober. He leaned heavily on Urban’s advice and support, knowing the older star had gone through the same thing. Vivien Killilea, Getty Images Keith Urban Keith Urban has been very open about his sobriety. He admits to struggling with alcohol and drugs just like his father did. Although he entered rehab a couple of times, he continued to relapse. Finally, in 2006 — shortly after marrying Nicole Kidman — Urban was urged to give rehab another try by his new bride, and he’s been sober ever since. His one regret is that he didn’t find a way to get sober sooner in his life. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Charles Kelley Lady A dropped a bombshell when they announced they would be canceling their 2022 Request Line Tour in order to support Charles Kelley’s journey to sobriety. After making jokes about his drinking for some time and ignoring the concerns of his bandmates, Kelley finally decided to make a change. One big motivator was his children starting to realize something was different about their father. Fast forward to today, Kelley is more than a year sober and in a much better place. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Chris Janson Sure, Chris Janson can “Fix a Drink” for you, but as for himself, he’ll stick with Mountain Dew. After years of drowning his sorrows in beer, he finally got sober. It was shortly after he met his wife Kelly Lynn in 2007 — ironically, in a bar. Janson was quick to stop drinking and hasn’t looked back since. He details his struggles with alcohol in his song "Holdin’ Her." Michael Reaves, Getty Images Jake Owen Jake Owen says life is so much better without alcohol. The bottle was slowly turning him into a person he didn’t want to be, but it was an embarrassing moment that had him sobering up real quick. Now, he’s celebrating years of abstaining from even a drop of alcohol. Jamie McCarthy, Getty Images Jason Isbell Jason Isbell has been an open book in his journey to sobriety. He has documented every step of both his addiction and recovery in his music. Like many male country singers who have gotten sober, he credits his wife Amanda Shires with pushing him in the right direction. The couple has been married since 2013. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Jo Dee Messina Attempting to keep the stressors of a country music career at bay, Jo Dee Messina turned to alcohol. But after years of battling an addiction, she had an eye-opening moment when she couldn’t remember the lyrics to one of her own songs while performing. Her manager confronted her, and shortly after that she entered a treatment facility in 2004 and has been sober ever since. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Jo Don Rooney In 2021, Joe Don Rooney was arrested for a DUI after he crashed his vehicle into a tree. It was that moment that put him on a path of sobriety. Now, more than two years sober, he’s taking each day as if it’s the only one he gets. The Rascal Flatts member admits that had he not had the wreck, he probably would have never taken responsibility for his life. Kevin Winter, Getty Images Joe Nichols The dependency on alcohol started at a very young age for Joe Nichols, who says he started drinking whiskey at age 13. It wasn’t until he walked down the aisle with his wife Heather Singleton in 2007 that he tried to make a change. He entered a rehab facility just 30 days after their wedding, but he couldn’t quite give it up. Finally, in 2008 — after an intervention from his family — Nichols made the commitment. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Jon Pardi Jon Pardi not only knows how to write a good drinking song, he has his own line of bourbon called Pardi Batch. But a medical exam in 2023 made him want to cut back significantly. Pardi revealed in December that he had retired from alcohol and was more than 100 day sober after finding out he was pre-diabetic. He made the decision after his doctor encouraged him to make some changes in his life. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Josh Turner Pointing to his faith, Josh Turner says he has never had a sip of alcohol. While many young people tend to rebel in certain ways, he says he opted to stay away from alcohol, drugs and cigarettes. Emma McIntyre, Getty Images Shania Twain Shania Twain is all about a clean lifestyle. In her biography, she talks about keeping her diet clean, so she abstains from drinking alcohol or partaking in drugs. She is also a vegetarian. These standards are also something that she expects from her band and team members. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Shay Mooney In 2023, Shay Mooney gave up alcohol completely. What started as a journey to lose weight in order to keep up with his kids turned into a complete lifestyle change. The Dan + Shay star stopped eating sugar and put the bottle back on the shelf. As a result, Mooney lost more than 50 pounds. Jamie McCarthy, Getty Images Tim McGraw Tim McGraw is the poster child of taking care of yourself. He committed to a life of fitness after seeing himself on screen in the movie Four Christmases , but his sobriety has been a part of his life for much longer. It was around that time in 2008 that his wife Faith Hill pushed him to make a change with his drinking habits. She told him simply it was taking over his life. Frazer Harrison, Getty Images Tyler Childers While Tyler Childers hasn’t said too much about his sobriety, he did touch on his lifestyle change in 2020. After releasing his album Long Violent History, he shared that he had given up drugs and alcohol six months prior. It appears he has kept his word over the years and he even talked about his sobriety at his New Year’s Eve show in 2023. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Walker Hayes Eight years ago, Walker Hayes was a completely different person — he refers to his old self as an "alcoholic atheist." Thanks to a man at a nearby church, a friend called Craig, Hayes began turning his life around: He found Jesus and he stopped drinking. Now, he’s been sober for more than eight years, but he still loves writing a good drinking song and has even found the lighter side of going to rehab, which he details in his song "AA." 4
